scenes.heading: Exhibit A: the sock

cues.text: Your robot vacuum promises to clean your home. But first, you may have to tidy up for your robot vacuum.
The court calls its first witness: a sock. It has been on the floor since Tuesday.
This is a fictional case, but the buying question is real: does this fit your routine?

scenes.note: Fictional household examples · Smart Choice 365 editorial judgement

scenes.heading: The buyer takes the stand
rows: I want help between big cleans
Check your floors and exact model

cues.text: The buyer says: I work all day. I want help keeping the floors under control between bigger cleans.
Fair argument. Repeated floor pickup is the job to consider, rather than a promise of a completely chore-free home.
Match the exact model to your floor types, rugs, layout and cleaning needs.

scenes.note: Fictional household examples · Smart Choice 365 editorial judgement

scenes.heading: Objection: the floor is occupied
rows: Pick up socks and small toys

cues.text: The opposition presents socks, toys and a charging cable. Your floor currently has more obstacles than a driving test.
Manufacturer guidance recommends clearing small items and securing loose cords before a run.
Obstacle avoidance varies by model. Do not assume a clever camera means you can ignore the preparation instructions.

scenes.note: Fictional household examples · Smart Choice 365 editorial judgement

scenes.heading: Witness for the defence: pet hair

cues.text: The defence calls a dog. No statement, just more hair on the floor.
If hair and crumbs build up often, regular floor pickup may be valuable to your household.
Compare suitable models, and check brush maintenance. Owning a pet is a reason to investigate, not an automatic verdict to buy.

scenes.note: Fictional household examples · Smart Choice 365 editorial judgement

scenes.heading: The staircase files an objection
rows: A floor robot has a defined job

cues.text: Now the staircase would like a word. Check the exact product's limits around stairs and changes in level.
For a conventional floor-cleaning robot, plan another way to clean stairs, furniture and places it cannot reach.
The useful question is what work it can take over in your home, not whether it replaces every cleaning tool.

scenes.note: Fictional household examples · Smart Choice 365 editorial judgement

scenes.heading: Exhibit B: the bits it cannot reach

cues.text: Before buying, check under-furniture clearance, tight spaces and the areas you actually want cleaned.
Navigation, edge cleaning and access differ by model and room layout.
Keep realistic expectations about manual touch-ups. This is a helper, not a live-in housekeeper.

scenes.note: Fictional household examples · Smart Choice 365 editorial judgement

scenes.heading: Self-emptying does not mean no care
rows: Bins, brushes and filters need care

cues.text: The maintenance witness has arrived. Apparently, the robot has chores for you as well.
Depending on the model, you will need to care for bins, brushes and filters. More elaborate docks can add other care tasks.
Check the manual, replacement supplies, warranty and ongoing costs before comparing the purchase price.

scenes.note: Fictional household examples · Smart Choice 365 editorial judgement

scenes.heading: Judge the routine, not the gadget
rows: Can you keep the floor ready?

cues.text: Picture an ordinary week. Can you keep the floor ready without turning it into a daily argument?
Would you run the robot regularly, rather than admire it parked beside the sofa?
And who will maintain it? Agree on that before the box arrives.

scenes.note: Fictional household examples · Smart Choice 365 editorial judgement

scenes.heading: The jury gets three questions

cues.text: Here is our editorial self-check, not a scientific score. Can you prepare the floor, use the robot regularly, and keep up with its care?
If the answers are yes, compare suitable models and total ownership costs.
If not, sort out the routine first. A simpler cleaning tool may fit better.

scenes.note: Editorial self-check · not a performance test or savings guarantee

scenes.heading: Verdict: a helper, with conditions

cues.text: The court finds that a robot vacuum may be a useful helper when the floor, routine and maintenance plan fit.
If your floor is permanently occupied and nobody wants the upkeep, pause before spending.
